questions.prompt: The standard contrast Hicks draws at the opening of this session is between:
choices: A Deductive reasoning and inductive reasoning.
B Ad hominem and modus ponens only.
C Geometry and music.
D Validity and Latin grammar.
questions.explain: The course so far focused on deduction; this lecture turns to induction as the usual contrast.

questions.prompt: In his chlorophyll vs. liars contrast, the inductive move is:
choices: A From a universal (“all plants…”) down to a particular fuchsia.
B From a sample of particulars (e.g. 280 chronic liars) out to a broader class.
C From an if-then to denying the antecedent.
D From a conclusion back to a premise indicator.
questions.explain: Deduction here goes from all plants to this plant; induction goes from 280 individuals to the whole class of chronic liars.

questions.prompt: The pasta-pot example is meant to show that induction is powerful because:
choices: A You must taste every piece to know the pot is done.
B Tasting one (cooled) piece licenses a generalization to the rest of the pot.
C Pasta proves modus tollens.
D Generalizations cannot be false.
questions.explain: You generalize from a particular tasting; you needn’t test each piece—then the caution is when such leaps go wrong.

questions.prompt: Unlike a typical deduction as Hicks describes it, inductive arguments:
choices: A Always contain the conclusion fully in the premises with certainty.
B Often cannot expect immediate certainty; generalization can be cautious and then stronger.
C Are identical to sound Barbara syllogisms.
D Are informal fallacies by definition.
questions.explain: Don’t demand certainty in all inductive arguments; you may generalize more cautiously, then more securely as study continues.

questions.prompt: The Semmelweis episode is used as a case of:
choices: A Pure categorical deduction with no observation.
B Open-ended discovery: noticing a priest, then a colleague’s matching symptoms, inside an observational/categorical scheme.
C Appeal to majority among hospital administrators.
D Affirming the consequent as a valid computer circuit.
questions.explain: He sees Kolletschka with the same symptoms as the dying women—an observation inside the categories he’s using, driving hypothesis revision.
